label.INDRESDEV: Total General Expenditure on Research and Development (GERD)

result.label: Indicator - Research and development
note:
[b]Research and development[/b]

[b]How do we measure this?[/b]
Total General Expenditure on Research and Development (GERD) in millions of pounds. Business expenditure (BERD) is measured through an annual survey of approximately 2,200 businesses in Northern Ireland. Government (GovERD) and Higher Education expenditure (HERD) is measured through a census of government departments, arm's length bodies and universities. GERD is the total of these three types of expenditure.

[b]Source[/b]
Research and Development Survey, NISRA
[url=https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/business/research-and-development]https://www.nisra.gov.uk/statistics/business/research-and-development[/url] 

[b]Impact of Covid-19[/b]
Data collection since the 2019 surveys occurred during and post-pandemic, this may have resulted in lower response rates in comparison to pre-Covid-19 surveys. Efforts were made to reduce the impact of a lower response rate. Namely, larger R&D contributors received more contact than usual to encourage a response and the survey response window was extended. As a result, 87% of total R&D spend in 2024 is covered by receipted businesses.

[b]Further information[/b]
1. As methodological improvements have been implemented for the 2022 survey, users should consider comparisons between pre-2022 BERD data and 2022 BERD data with caution.
2. GDP deflator used to convert current prices to constant prices: 2011 (71.0), 2012 (72.1), 2013 (73.7), 2014 (74.9), 2015 (75.4), 2016 (76.7), 2017 (77.8), 2018 (79.4), 2019 (81.3), 2020 (85.4), 2021 (85.9), 2022 (90.7), 2023 (96.5), 2024 (100.0).
Source: [url=https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/gdp-deflators-at-market-prices-and-money-gdp-september-2025-quarterly-national-accounts]GDP deflators at market prices, and money GDP September 2025 (Quarterly National Accounts)[/url]
3. For the 2023 estimates, NISRA updated the classification of some businesses conducting R&D that also received Invest NI support. This reclassification was applied during the grossing and estimation stage and will be incorporated into the sampling strategy in future surveys. NISRA believes this approach provides a more accurate reflection of R&D performance in Northern Ireland.
